policy: A caught product failure must gain a reproducible production-path test/type/lint guard before resolution. These historical defects have executable test guards. New failed runs emit regression-candidates.json and stay red; candidates are not automatically declared fixed or counted as tests. Native guards remain not-run until executed on macOS.

Vocabulary prompt echo could be inserted as speech.
Late target translation overwrote current language.
Clear allowed pending old recognition to reappear.
Stop/target recovery missed captions while producer drained.
Permission-setup buffers could reach meeting content.
Unknown external microphone owner was silently ignored.
Host uptime created leading recording time.
Late drawing word cues revived cancelled timeline.

Typing continued after user focus drift.
Ultron additive oscillator injected tone into silent pauses.

Forgotten evidence could reconnect memory pages.
Opening recap source could disturb an active session.
Completion could reveal before final persistence succeeded.

Microphone callback copied samples before mute admission.
Meetings and Recordly feedback models could diverge after stop; pure temporal contract now shared (native wing wiring remains a separate unverified obligation).
Elapsed processing time could imply success before saved output.
Unreadable accessibility subrole passed a not-equal-secure check and could permit replacement.
A skipped, cancelled, missing, or unsuccessful prerequisite could escape a check aggregate.

Duplicate JSON keys or non-finite values could disguise a failed or malformed receipt.
Partial Recordly export output could emit whole-export completion feedback.
Native Scribe save/retry could claim completion before durable notes, or drop newer private notes.
A positive native test total could hide an omitted required regression case on every push.
Positively active microphone input with unresolved PID or bundle identity was discarded, allowing a later empty scan to restore capture.
Native Path flattening failed Apple Swift type-checking; the typed refactor must preserve actual Bezier endpoints and midpoint geometry.
Cloud finish closures captured shadowing locals before declaration; completion must retain the actual missing-key failure.
Native feedback attempted to set read-only accessibility environment values; explicit render/style inputs must retain reduced-motion frame stability.
Generated portable packages omitted the production macOS deployment floor, so real Mac CI rejected otherwise available concurrency and Foundation APIs.
macOS /var temporary-path aliases caused the input snapshot to include its own output receipt and falsely report changed source.
The aggregate gate rejected a valid generated source package when the trusted output ancestor used the macOS /var to /private/var alias.
A single native compiler failure repeatedly rebuilt the identical failing target for every fixture suite; the shared barrier must block all native test execution while keeping each obligation unmet.
Native --skip-build results could be accepted without a successful compiler barrier for the exact current source snapshot.
Portable exact-declaration excerpts omitted the original CoreGraphics import, so native Mac compilation rejected CGRect.zero, default geometry arguments and Equatable synthesis.
The native Scribe control journey attempted activation before its owned button became enabled; waiting must stay bounded and must not bypass a permanently disabled control.

Actual Mac component QA could not find the production scribe.start control in the owned accessibility tree; the real button journey must execute successfully rather than treating controller calls or a positive suite total as equivalent.
ScreenshotDetector ignored its injected defaults and read host preferences instead.
BrowserAgentBrainLaunch discarded injected model preferences for non-Claude engines.
Successful console totals could mask a missing, stale or changed app-native receipt.
Swift Testing human summaries can report a passing positive total even when disabled or empty-argument tests were skipped.
A parameterized function-level pass could hide an omitted compiled argument identity.
Compiled discovery could omit current Core declarations while a smaller selected test set still produced a positive total.
An unselected app suite could execute without selected child tests while every required function still passed.
A passing native function stream could omit selected suite lifecycles or include declarations after the terminal run event.
An injected onboarding animation preference could negate the system Reduce Motion setting.
Native artifact collection rejected macOS temporary output roots entered through /var when resolved children lived under /private/var.
Source review found Memory cancellation policy reading host preferences instead of the injected fixture cancellation IDs.
Source review found Memory source navigation initializing the live Scribe singleton, including its call watcher, instead of using an isolated navigation port.
Source review of the first native reference adaptation found the beam clock restarting on processing and completion label changes.
Actual Swift Testing list output omits argument expansion, so requiring argument IDs during function discovery blocked all parameterized native execution.
Actual Swift Testing list output omits implicit suite declarations that execution emits for compiler-discovered function containers.
Source review found completed feedback could keep requesting high-refresh frames until the five-second notice expiry after its visible transition had finished.
Source review found a paused or Reduce Motion display clock could reuse an old timestamp and hide a later completed state.
Independent source review found fixed wall/media epochs could hide newly completed states after a system wall-clock correction.
Source review found a provider asset test could pass using the source-tree file even if the actual app bundle omitted that asset.
Source review found failed Keychain deletion could clear cached state and let settings report removal even though the backend retained the secret.
Actual macOS execution and an exact-source resolver fixture found normalized x.ai and Ollama (local) aliases incorrectly falling back instead of using provider marks.
A synchronous local-socket reply to a non-reading peer blocked MainActor; the deliberate synchronous-writer regression control exceeded the 250 ms budget.
The full macOS test run failed before either router contention sink entered while deliberately blocking workers depended on the shared global dispatch pool.
Independent source review found invisible future transcript text still reserving layout height and scrolling the eligible prefix away.
The original MCP codec trapped with signal 4 when an untrusted response ID was a finite numeric value outside Int range.
The original MCP codec trapped with signal 4 when an untrusted error code was a finite numeric value outside Int range.
Source review found repeated mute watchdog replacement could accumulate blocked synchronous readers without a global bound.
Source review found partial license credential deletion could lose cleanup state across relaunch and restore activation from retained credentials.
Actual macOS onboarding fixture could not find packaged app resources when SwiftPM placed the resource bundle beside the loaded XCTest bundle.
Source review found a blocked child stdin write could monopolize the MCP actor and prevent deadline or cancellation from closing the transport.
Parallel stdio fixtures exposed inherited pipe descriptors that kept EOF open after the owning child exited.
Independent source review found an in-flight background license activation response could restore credentials after explicit deactivation.
Source review found malformed complete MCP output could be ignored until request timeout instead of closing the invalid transport.
Source review found a duplicate Chrome bridge request ID could replace the original pending reply instead of rejecting only the duplicate.
Independent event-driver review found that a native control beneath an alpha-zero ancestor could pass readiness checks and receive a click despite being invisible.

Combined app test execution shared process-global snapshot/window state across unrelated suites; actual macOS fixtures observed stalled readiness while another suite changed global presentation policy.
The actual combined native process exited zero without a Swift Testing summary or runEnded, leaving selected cases incomplete after unrelated suites had passed.
Exact-source local-helper probes reproduced stdin writes blocking before the timeout watchdog could run.
Exact-source local-helper probes reproduced a SIGTERM-ignoring child exceeding its deadline and still returning a successful status.
Source review found wake and research diagnostics could record conversation text without explicit content logging being enabled.
Source review found provider errors could reach voice diagnostic sinks before a single shared credential and home-path redaction step.
Independent diagnostic review found character-based truncation could retain unbounded bytes in one grapheme and could split a credential before redaction.
The original native bridge executable accepted an oversized UInt32 frame length and waited for the declared body instead of promptly settling the pending local request.
The original native bridge executable blocked writing stdout before registering its request timeout, stranding pending local sockets while stdin remained open.
A deliberate clean-EOF probe caught the first asynchronous bridge repair cancelling an already accepted response instead of flushing it before exit.
Independent source review found stopping native input before dispatch-source setup could omit its terminal callback or notify before closing the owned descriptor.

Source review found a rejected or untested remote cleartext endpoint could remain enabled and send the prompt and key; restoring unguarded request construction reproduces the leak in synthetic fixtures.
A deliberate redirect-following mutation delivered a synthetic prompt and key to the redirect destination instead of preserving the original endpoint boundary.
Source review found edits and preset changes could retain approval from a previous endpoint and stale validation results could restore that approval.
Source review found an unknown provider authentication result was displayed as signed in.
Source review found disabling every offered agent silently restored Claude as a fallback.
Source review found installed Cursor and Gemini offers did not consistently follow their individual integration switches.
Source review found opening a chat provider app was described as handing off the prompt even though that handoff was unsupported.
Source review found the Anthropic Messages API listed as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint preset.
The original local voice worker probe returned a WAV path while its producer was still writing incomplete audio bytes.
The original local voice worker probe ignored task cancellation and kept synthesis running instead of promptly returning no artifact.
Independent review of the voice-worker repair found a validated file descriptor could be replaced by moving the subsequently reopened pathname.
Independent review of the voice-worker repair found a RIFF prefix alone could be accepted without complete PCM format, chunk bounds and alignment.
Independent review of the voice-worker repair found cancellation was checked before artifact copying but not during the copy or before final handoff.
A generated 44-byte WAV with a declared format body beyond the available bytes crashed the original decoder with SIGILL instead of returning failure.
An original-source timer probe showed releasing TickClock without disappear left its scheduled run-loop timer valid.
Source review found cloud-only warm work could inspect local voice settings and render Kokoro; an unconditional-warm mutation reproduces the unwanted action.
Source review found local voice warm-up could run a ready Kokoro model even when another voice provider was selected or the provider was paused.
Source review found onboarding polling ownership was not tied to visible-window intervals and teardown.
Actual macOS bridge fixtures rejected closed readers because the test assumed Linux writer-POLLERR readiness semantics on Darwin.

The native pipe-stop fixture measured observer resumption rather than the worker callback, so its observed delay could not distinguish actual transport latency from delayed test-executor scheduling; the guard now measures callback completion with the unchanged 500 ms bound.
Independent mutation review showed stop-before-start fixtures did not establish descriptor-closure ordering for an already active native input source.
Actual macOS test compilation printed an internal corrupted-JSON error, then exited zero with Build complete; compiler diagnostics must remain blocking despite that exit status.
Adding a valid WAV native obligation exposed a selftest that assumed the final obligation was device proof; the test must remove each actual evidence tier independently of map order.

Actual concurrent Core execution outlasted the mute fixture's five-second automatic semaphore release, invalidating its still-blocked-reader premise before the observer resumed; the same failure was reproduced with a delayed continuation.

The macOS endpoint fixture failed before obtaining its Python port file; the precise startup cause is unproved. Owned bind/listen readiness and explicit cleanup replace competing startup/helper lifetimes without extending the HTTP deadline.
Native event dispatch removed and rejected an unrelated queued mouse-up after AppKit had already consumed its own release.
The AX readiness fixture rejected a transient unknown role immediately, before its existing readiness budget could resolve a valid button; persistent wrong roles must still never receive a press.
Actual production compilation exited zero after internal compiler errors, but the app build step and aggregate gate accepted the command outcome without inspecting its compiler diagnostics.
The original compiler matcher classified a Swift warning's source excerpt containing an error: argument as a compiler error.
Independent review reproduced a passing aggregate receipt after inserting an internal compiler error into the final bundle compilation log and refreshing its hash.
Independent static review found the diagnostic header parser no longer rejected LLVM ERROR and absolute compiler-path headers that the previous matcher blocked.

The new CLI regression printed expected error diagnostics into unittest's result line, preventing the strict runner from identifying every reported test. Capture and assert those diagnostics inside the fixture.
Actual AppKit queue insertion narrowed a synthetic event number and rounded its timestamp, so the native journey driver rejected its own queued release as unrelated.
The wrong-ID and wrong-path worker fixtures also used invalid WAV data, allowing unrelated WAV rejection or startup failure to stand in for the intended protocol guard.
A throwing worker fixture removed its directory before cancelling and joining the render task and closing its worker; failed assertions could discard diagnostics while work was still using them.
